title: Sharp Average Treatment Effect Frontiers under Average-Case Pearson Sensitivity Budgets
banked_reason: D0.5 panels PASS with no findings, but the general referee assigns subfield at 7.1 below the 7.4 field floor and marks the package not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The inference result does not deliver the tangent/bootstrap procedure introduced in the definitions and remains confined to a uniformly Slater-regular region whose nonemptiness and empirical checkability are not demonstrated for the proposed application.
The Ishikawa–He–Kanamori comparison is correctly only against the note-defined box-augmented specialization, so it does not establish a gap relative to their full published class.
No NHANES or other substantive application is delivered, limiting the demonstrated econometric importance and keeping the projected leading-journal score below the strongest field contributions.
proof_attempt_summary: Six D0 solve rounds produced a clean theorem graph for the sharp compatible-full-law frontier, binary garbling reduction, scalar catalog, exact box-augmented comparator gap, regular-region confidence diameter, and boundary impossibility result; both substantive D0.5 panels passed with no findings. The field-tier framing failed because support-changing tangent/bootstrap inference, comparison against the unqualified published IHK class, and the proposed empirical application remain substantial undelivered extensions, leaving the sound package at subfield tier.
tldr: A finite observed law is lifted to one joint law of treatment and both potential outcomes, and the least Pearson assignment information needed to support each ATE is profiled. The attained sharp frontier has a perspective SOCP and explicit dual. For binary outcomes, a treatment-independent garbling removes the minority discordant response type without imposing monotone treatment response and without increasing any convex assignment cost; this yields the complete six-face scalar catalog and a squared-correlation null identity. A one-way, cost-nonincreasing embedding into the explicitly defined box-augmented Neyman specialization of Ishikawa--He--Kanamori equation~(14) gives the exact separation \(9/70>9/91\); strict interiority and continuity extend it to a nonempty open neighborhood with a uniformly positive gap. On a named uniformly Slater-regular multinomial region, a fixed-odds-cone parametrization, a uniform equality right inverse, and bounded attained cellwise dual multipliers yield a finite-sample \(O(n^{-1/2})\) profile diameter without transporting a dual certificate between laws; a contiguous boundary pair shows that honest bands must retain infinite diameter at a finite-to-infinite null-cost boundary.
gap: Average-case sensitivity analysis has sharp armwise potential-outcome bounds but no jointly attained ATE frontier. Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's published \(f\)-divergence computation uses Jensen and conditional-moment relaxations whose cross-world realizability is unresolved. Existing inference theory does not quantify both the regular finite-sample width and the finite-to-infinite boundary obstruction for this frontier.
fill: The project profiles the exact full-law Pearson cost, certifies it by primal and dual conic programs, solves the binary geometry, embeds the full-law model into the published Jensen--CMC program with identical budget normalization, and pairs a finite-sample regular-region diameter theorem with a contiguous boundary lower bound.
